To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inclusion of “low salt” (i.e. 0.3g/100g) in bread is a practical way to achieve a reduction in dietary salt in a pragmatic dietary setting and that a modest reduction in salt intake, in the context of a dietary approach that included a “low-salt bread” as a component of a reduced-salt diet, resulted in a significant reduction in systolic BP, but not diatolic BP.
the consumption of “low-sat” bread as part a pragmatic reduced-sat diet can lead to a clinically significant reduction in systolic BP in adults with elevated BP.

a modest reduction in salt intake, which included the use of “Low-Salt” bread, resulted in a significant, and potentially clinically important, reduction in systolic blood pressure in adults with mildly elevated blood pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a pragmatic reduced salt diet for lowering BP.

the effects of dietary salt reduction on blood pressure and other cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors, and the development of strategies and interventions to help reduce salt intake in the general population.
the role of dietary salt in health, and the development of practical dietary interventions that can be used to reduce salt intake in the general population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inclusion of “low salt bread” as part of a reduced-salt diet is a useful and practical strategy for lowering systolic BP in adults with elevated BP.
the use of “Low-Salt” bread as a key component of a reduced-salt diet can be an effective and practical strategy for lowering BP in adults with elevated BP.
a modest reduction in salt intake, in the range of 1.7–2.0 g/day, can be achieved by the use of “Low-Salt” bread as an important component of a pragmatic reduced salt dietary intervention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inclusion of low-salt bread in a pragmatic reduced-saltdietary strategy can be effective in lowering blood pressure.

the consumption of “low-salts” bread as part and parcel of a reduced-salt diet can be an important component of a pragmatic approach for reducing dietary salt intake and lowering BP in mildly to moderately hypertensive adults.

the use of “Low-Salt” bread is an important component of a pragmatic, reduced-salt diet for lowering BP, and that the inclusion of “Low-Salts” bread in the diet of adults with elevated BP, as part of a comprehensive approach to dietary salt reduction, should be considered as a public health strategy for reducing the burden of elevated BP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bread can play an important role in the reduction of dietary salt intake, and thus in the management of hypertension.
“low-salt”, or “very-low-salt”, bread is a viable option for inclusion as part of an overall reduced-salt dietary strategy to lower BP in adults.
bread is a very important component of a pragmatic dietary strategy for lowering BP in adults with elevated BP.
